label: D&D 5e
description: Dungeons & Dragons, 5th Edition — the classic fantasy TTRPG.
tldr: D&D 5e — the benchmark tabletop RPG. Four actions per round (action, bonus action, movement, reaction) on a d20 grid: roll under a DC or meet a target. Six abilities (Str/Dex/Con/Int/Wis/Cha) drive derived modifiers and skill checks. Each class level grants at least one feature — that's your 'buff tree'. Damage types and saving throws (six, ability-based) do most of the narrative lifting, so describe the physical outcome of every roll.

races.Human: Ambitious, adaptable, and everywhere. Humans are the youngest and boldest of the common folk — whatever they lack in longevity they make up for in sheer drive.
races.Elf: Elegant and long-lived, elves carry centuries of grace and sorrow in their step. Otherworldly beauty hides an unshakable composure and a deep love of art and magic.
races.Dwarf: Stout, stubborn, and unbreakable as the mountains they call home. Dwarves measure wealth in craftsmanship and friendship in oaths kept.
races.Halfling: Small folk with big appetites and bigger hearts. Halflings prize comfort, community, and good food — and survive by luck others call providence.
races.Dragonborn: Born of dragons and proud of it. Dragonborn wear their elemental ancestry on their scaled hides and a breath of fire or frost on their lips.
races.Gnome: Tiny tinkers and endless enthusiasts. Gnomes chase every idea with gleeful energy, turning gadgets, illusions, and mischief into an art form.
races.Half-Elf: Caught between two worlds, half-elves belong fully to neither — and so become diplomats, wanderers, and friends to all.
races.Half-Orc: Strength and fury tempered by surprising tenderness. Half-orcs balance the wild violence of their orc blood against very human loyalties.
races.Tiefling: Marked by an infernal bloodline, tieflings bear horns, tails, and wary glances. Their heritage is a burden, but it grants resolve forged in fire.

classes.Barbarian: Rage made flesh. Barbarians trade finesse for fury, shrugging off wounds that would fell lesser folk as they answer injury with eruption.
classes.Bard: A maestro of magic, music, and mayhem. Bards weave spells through song and wit, turning every tavern, court, and battlefield into a stage.
classes.Cleric: A chosen vessel of the divine. Clerics channel their god's will into healing, blessing, and blinding holy light.
classes.Druid: A guardian of the old wilds. Druids speak the language of beast and branch, shifting shape and calling the fury of nature to their side.
classes.Fighter: Master of every weapon they touch. Fighters are the unglamorous backbone of any battle — and the reason the rest survive it.
classes.Monk: Discipline sharpened into a weapon. Monks fight with the body itself, moving with supernatural speed and striking with focused ki.
classes.Paladin: Oath-bound and radiant. Paladins are living armor of their convictions, smiting evil and shielding the innocent with equal zeal.
classes.Ranger: A hunter with one foot in the wild. Rangers track, trap, and guide — the unseen edge between a party and certain ambush.
classes.Rogue: A shadow with quick hands and quicker wits. Rogues open what's locked, find what's hidden, and strike where it hurts most.
classes.Sorcerer: Magic from the blood, not the book. Sorcerers bend raw power that was born in them, shaping it by instinct and will.
classes.Warlock: A bargain struck with something older than the world. Warlocks wield borrowed power — and the price is always due.
classes.Wizard: Magic from study, patience, and relentless intellect. Wizards bend reality through ritual and formula, unlocking spells with discipline alone.
